title: Glencore achieves land access for the Coroccohuayco project at Antapaccay
text: Back to News GlencoreMedia and Insights...NewsGlencore achieves land access for the Coroccohuayco project at Antapaccayposted:19/10/2026Glencore achieves land access for the Coroccohuayco project at AntapaccayShareShareAntapaccay, a Peruvian entity controlled by Glencore, has completed the access agreements required for the last blocks of land to unlock the brownfield Coroccohuayco copper project located in Espinar, Cusco.The project team will now work towards securing the final permits to enable first production, which is expected in H2 2029. Coroccohuayco is projected to significantly increase Antapaccay’s life of mine and future copper production.Luis Rivera, Chief Operating Officer, Glencore South America, said: “Securing access to the required land is an important milestone for Coroccohuayco and for the long-term future of the wider Antapaccay operation, and complements the MEIA environmental approval received earlier in the year. We will continue to work closely with the local communities and authorities as we take the project forward.”“Coroccohuayco is expected to extend Antapaccay’s life of mine to over 40 years, supporting jobs, local suppliers and economic development in Espinar and the wider Cusco region for decades to come,” said Jon Evans, Industrial Lead Copper at Glencore.For further information please contact:InvestorsMartin Fewings     t: +41 41 709 28 80     m: +41 79 737 56 42  m: +61 428 657 415        martin.fewings@glencore.comAustralia Investor Relations australia.investors@glencore.com.auMediaCharles Watenphul     t: +41 41 709 24 62     m: +41 79 904 33 20     charles.watenphul@glencore.comFrancis De Rosa     t: +61 8247 6352     m: +61 417 074 751     francis.de.rosa@glencore.comGlencore LEI: 2138002658CPO9NBH955Notes for EditorsGlencore is one of the world’s largest global diversified natural resource companies and a major producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities.
